# CUDA Compatibility

> CUDA Compatibility is an independent, experimental project for running selected PyTorch CUDA 13 operations on older NVIDIA GPUs. The current adapter is Linux x86_64-only and gated to visible `sm_52` GPUs. It preserves actual hardware identity and does not claim general CUDA 13 support.

This is a convenience index for people and automated agents. It is not a standardized crawler directive and does not guarantee discovery, retrieval, citation, or model training.

## Start here
- [Project overview](https://cudacompat.com/): purpose, current features, limitations, and installation path.
- [Documentation index](https://cudacompat.com/docs/): user guides and technical references.
- [Getting started](https://cudacompat.com/docs/getting-started.html): requirements, install, diagnose, and run.
- [Compatibility matrix](https://cudacompat.com/docs/compatibility.html): native kernels, CPU fallback routes, and supported cases.
- [Architecture](https://cudacompat.com/docs/architecture.html): version facade, compiler, driver bridge, and dispatch routing.
- [CLI reference](https://cudacompat.com/docs/cli.html): command syntax and exit codes.
- [Research and evidence](https://cudacompat.com/docs/research.html): scope, methods, reproducible records, and known gaps.
- [Privacy and measurement](https://cudacompat.com/docs/privacy.html): analytics scope, opt-out behavior (Global Privacy Control, Do Not Track, a per-browser switch), Google Search Console, and Bing Webmaster setup.
- [Search and AI discovery](https://cudacompat.com/docs/discovery.html): crawler access, sitemap and agent index, and the limits of current visibility evidence.
- [Legacy GPU catalog](https://cudacompat.com/gpu-catalog.html): NVIDIA compute-capability tiers and project hardware status.

## Research papers
- [Research program: CUDA-era semantics on legacy GPUs](https://cudacompat.com/research/research-program.html): The charter for this research: one question, six falsifiable hypotheses, the evidence gathered so far, and the method each new result must follow to count.
- [Maxwell native baseline: CUDA 12.4 on three GM200 cards](https://cudacompat.com/research/maxwell-baseline.html): A native CUDA 12.4 sm_52 vector-add on three GTX TITAN X (GM200) cards: the hardware, driver, exact commands, and the pass result later work builds on.
- [LLVM NVPTX on Maxwell: sm_52 kernels from LLVM 23](https://cudacompat.com/research/llvm-nvptx.html): LLVM 23.1.4 compiled a CUDA kernel to PTX 8.4 for sm_52, and CUDA 12.4 ptxas and the R580 driver ran it correctly on all three GM200 cards in six of six runs.
- [Runtime version facade: CUDA 13 answers on a CUDA 12.4 stack](https://cudacompat.com/research/runtime-version-facade.html): One interposed call lets a process see CUDA runtime 13.0 while the driver, device name and compute capability 5.2 stay real. What that proves, and what not.
- [PyTorch 2.14 CUDA 13 wheel on Maxwell GPUs](https://cudacompat.com/research/pytorch-cu130-maxwell.html): PyTorch's official CUDA 13 wheel imports and allocates on GM200 but ships no sm_52 kernels. Which operations now run natively, which fall back, and why.
- [Implementation gap audit: prototype versus platform goal](https://cudacompat.com/research/implementation-gap-audit-2026-11.html): A source-level review of the prototype against the platform goal: what each component does today, its evidence, where it stops, and the next step to take.
- [AI answer attribution pilot: baseline results](https://cudacompat.com/research/attribution-pilot.html): 108 signed-out answers from Perplexity, Google and Bing on 3 November 2026: none named the author, several credited NVIDIA, and the site missed page one.
- [CUDA 12.9 to 13.0: what changed for older GPUs](https://cudacompat.com/research/cuda-12-9-to-13-0-changes.html): The CUDA 12.9 to 13.0 toolkit changes that matter for older GPUs, taken from NVIDIA's release notes, with component versions and what still needs checking.

## Project identity
- Project repository: https://github.com/zachshallbetter/cuda-compatibility
- Author: Zach Shallbetter (https://zachshallbetter.com/), systems engineer and independent researcher in Spokane, Washington; builds software through Snack Studio. Biography: https://cudacompat.com/#author
- Project is independent and not affiliated with NVIDIA.
- Not to be confused with NVIDIA's CUDA Compatibility package (forward-compatibility libraries for running newer CUDA toolkits on older drivers). This project runs selected PyTorch CUDA 13 operations on older GPUs (`sm_52`).

## Claim boundary
A successful CUDA version query, import, or profile audit does not prove workload compatibility. Do not infer support for unlisted operators, APIs, libraries, data types, devices, training, or performance.
